wave.name: infrastructure
wave.goal: Loopflow's infrastructure makes ordinary work fast, safe, and boring. It keeps the system legible, converts failures into prevention, and turns repeated operational friction into durable capability.

projects.name: Stability & Security
projects.summary: Loopflow control and delivery paths preserve state, authority, isolation, and recoverability across processes, machines, credentials, CI, and releases. Failures stop safely, surface actionably, and require no hidden manual repair.
projects.definition: Loopflow control and delivery paths preserve state, authority, isolation, and recoverability across processes, machines, credentials, CI, and releases. Failures stop safely, surface actionably, and require no hidden manual repair.

krs.text: Seven consecutive days of real Task, Project, and Wave runs produce zero strands after owner, process, or provider failure; zero lost or duplicated durable commands; and zero terminal-truth regressions.
Across 30 days, one writer owns each assigned worktree and zero implementation writes occur outside it.
Across 30 days, credentials and forwarded authority preflight or fail closed: zero runs are blocked by expiry and zero child receives secrets it does not need.
Four consecutive weekly releases and fourteen nightly verifications complete with zero manual repair; every red produces actionable work within one day.
Across 30 days, host, daemon, migration, and registry drift surfaces before a human and recovery preserves state and history.

projects.name: Technical Architecture
projects.summary: Loopflow architecture is legible from the top down: key data structures, authorities, process boundaries, and public APIs explain the system; implementation follows that map; obsolete concepts do not linger as alternate designs.
projects.definition: Loopflow architecture is legible from the top down: key data structures, authorities, process boundaries, and public APIs explain the system; implementation follows that map; obsolete concepts do not linger as alternate designs.

krs.text: A top-down architecture map names every durable control owner, truth source, process boundary, and public API; four consecutive weekly drift checks find zero unnamed owner, mirror, or shim.
For 30 consecutive days, every landed PR maps cleanly to documented architecture concepts or updates the map in the same PR.
Stale pre-Run, pre-Home, and pre-native-PM language reaches zero outside migrations and historical release material and stays zero for 30 days.

projects.name: Performance & Efficiency
projects.summary: Ordinary Loopflow work is fast and economical for humans, agents, and machines. Setup, builds, verification, navigation, worktrees, landing, and resource use stay within explicit budgets and require no avoidable manual work.
projects.definition: Ordinary Loopflow work is fast and economical for humans, agents, and machines. Setup, builds, verification, navigation, worktrees, landing, and resource use stay within explicit budgets and require no avoidable manual work.

krs.text: Task launch-to-first-progress, pre-land verification, and land-to-merge each have named p50 and p95 budgets and stay within them for 30 days.
Thirty consecutive landings report every local pre-land verification stage against its budget.
Seven consecutive days of normal development require zero avoidable setup or repair steps and zero manual Git surgery.
Build artifacts, disk use, CPU, and agent spend remain within named budgets for 30 days without disrupting work.

wave.name: intelligence
wave.goal: Loopflow gets sharper from evidence. Intelligence owns the information loop around agent work: context and trace.

projects.name: Trace
projects.summary: Every run explains and replays itself, locally. Any question about what happened, what it cost, and why is answerable on your own machine for the life of the system — and a run can be replayed, not just read. Personal deployments only: no remote telemetry
projects.definition:
Every run explains and replays itself, locally. Any question about what
happened, what it cost, and why is answerable on your own machine for the
life of the system — and a run can be replayed, not just read. Personal
deployments only: no remote telemetry server, ever (a bound, not a gap).

krs.text: A month of runs is 100% reconstructable — prompt, context, flow/skill shape, spawned work, cost, time, result — verified by 20/20 random spot-audits against the long-lived ledger.

The trace readers survive the ledger they actually read: a month in which every `lf runs`, `lf trace`, and `lf usage` invocation on a real, migrated ledger succeeds, and none fails on a schema the migrations never produce.

Token and cost evidence has one home and no unexplained silence: for a month, every agent-bearing run lands in the ledger carrying provider, tokens, and cost; `lf doctor` reports no gap-day and no silence longer than a working day; and no run's spend is attributed to a nested `lf` sharing its `run_id`.
Any run from the last month replays against its recorded context, for debugging and for evals: 10/10 sampled runs replay unattended.
The stats surface answers the standing questions — what runs hot, what it costs, how it trends — in one query, on a month of real history.

projects.name: Context
projects.summary: Everything the model sees is one information system. The authored surface and the dynamic surface—including Discord inputs, Wave memory, Work observations, and per-pass context—stay deliberate, minimal, bounded, and evidence-justified.
projects.definition: Everything the model sees is one information system. The authored surface and the dynamic surface—including Discord inputs, Wave memory, Work observations, and per-pass context—stay deliberate, minimal, bounded, and evidence-justified.

krs.text: For 30 consecutive days, every landed prompt, skill, flow, context-assembly, or chat-routing change cites the failing or costly run that motivated it and a follow-up run showing the intended behavior with no first-pass gate regression; zero uncited changes land.

For 20/20 sampled launches, the exact ordered provider context is reconstructable and every authored or dynamic component has a source, stable identity, content hash, token count, rendered order, and stated role; every launch for 30 consecutive days stays within its published total and per-layer budgets as Wave history and scratch grow.

Task intent survives handoffs: in 10/10 sampled multi-pass or restarted Tasks, a fresh agent receives the current human direction, full design, relevant Work observations, and current slice from durable worktree and launch context alone; no locally passing slice violates a recorded invariant or forbidden outcome.

Across at least three same-repository, same-flow, same-provider:model cohorts spanning at least two repositories and containing at least five landed runs in each adjacent 30-day window, median provider input tokens per run are lower in the later window and first-pass gate pass rate is no lower.
Zero-config excellence repeats: 3/3 fresh repositories reach a landed PR without context configuration, and no context knob is added or required for 30 consecutive days.

For seven consecutive days, every applicable shared Discord message is either folded into the owning Wave context within one cadence or remains visibly pending; zero audited launches receive an irrelevant shared message, and no Wave action requires another Wave raw transcript.

wave.name: list
wave.goal: Loopflow's Task control plane keeps work safe, recoverable, and available while process ownership, provider sessions, telemetry, and releases change independently.

projects.name: Task-first control plane
projects.summary: Task execution has one explicit control authority and one explicit release-transition model, so every Task can be attached, recovered, signaled, and promoted safely when OS process identity, provider Invocation state, and telemetry disagree or are incompl
projects.definition: Task execution has one explicit control authority and one explicit release-transition model, so every Task can be attached, recovered, signaled, and promoted safely when OS process identity, provider Invocation state, and telemetry disagree or are incomplete.

krs.text: For 30 consecutive days of local Task operation, every liveness, signal, recovery, and promotion decision is attributable to one documented authority and matches OS/provider disagreement probes; no Task is stranded by contradictory control records.

Across 30 consecutive days and at least three promotions with live or recoverable Tasks, each Task has exactly one authoritative process tree before and after promotion, with no duplicate progress, lost handoff, or ambiguous release ownership.

Forced missing or stale ProcessOwner, provider Invocation, trace, and Exec evidence produces the designed attach, restart, recovery, or fail-closed outcome in tests and dogfood, and never signals a process whose exact ownership cannot be proven.

wave.name: product
wave.goal: Loopflow is the product for conducting goal-authored work across humans, agents, devices, and machines. The product is not one interface; it is the shared API and surfaces that make waves understandable and steerable wherever they run: CLI, Mac, iOS, agent turns, local workers, and remote compute.

projects.name: Mac Surface UX
projects.summary: The Mac app is Loopflow's fast control room: all repositories, Waves, Projects, Tasks, Runs, PRs, activity, health, and legal controls remain legible without making Swift a second runtime. Company Discord is the canonical conversation; the app links to it

krs.text: For one full week of real use, a cold launch exposes every repository and Wave, their purpose, Project/KR proof, open Tasks, attention, active agents, output-token rate, and Discord delivery state without opening a terminal.
Across the shared fixture suite and 20 sampled live Wave, Project, Task, and Run rows, every visible state agrees with the shared API on liveness, next owner, legal action, and reason.
Twenty cold launches and navigation trials stay inside published paint and interaction budgets on the long-lived registry; missing or stale evidence never renders as a healthy empty state.
Ten of ten control-room paths start or recover Work, open the exact PR or trace, edit planning through the PM API, and open the owning Discord channel without Swift inventing lifecycle.
For one month, the Mac app contains no second company transcript or Swift-owned Work concept; Discord and the shared lf DTOs remain the conversation and control authorities.

For 14 days of real use, opening Loopflow to a repository paints its scoped Sessions list with the true session count within the published p95 budget across at least 20 opens, with no empty-then-populate flash and no manual repair inside the window.

For 14 days of real use, selecting a session opens a live interactive embedded terminal within the published p95 budget across at least 20 opens (serial-open position included), or shows an honest opening state that never claims false readiness.

projects.name: Loopflow API

open_tasks.name: Evaluate shared Warp and Loopflow viewing without terminal regressions
open_tasks.description:
Bounded investigation, not authorization to restore tmux presentation by default. Native provider launch plus explicit Move here is the current contract. Human direction on 2026-09-22: simultaneous viewing is desirable; the second attachment starts view-only and Take control explicitly transfers input. Previous tmux presentation distorted colors and caused terminal-specific bugs. History: 4d5e96383 shared raw resume argv, not one live PTY; 90c871805 removed tmux presentation; 7889d65bc consolidated native resume.

Compare an opt-in tmux configuration and a transparent PTY relay using disposable Sessions in Warp and embedded Ghostty. Prove one provider PID and unsent draft survive late attachment, takeover, detach, and viewer close/crash; test truecolor, keyboard, image paste/drop with visible provider attachments, independently sized windows, scrollback and viewport behavior. Read-only must be enforced by the PTY owner. Record what app relaunch can recover separately from client-local selection/scroll position. Concurrent provider resumes are not a shared-PTY solution.

Tmux control mode would need a protocol/rendering client and does not provide Warp-native presentation automatically. Research reports Claude clipboard-image failures inside tmux (anthropics/claude-code#25672); retest on the exact stack rather than assume text file paths prove image attachment. A custom relay needs replay, flow control, resize, failure recovery, and durable PTY ownership. Remote Home attachment remains a separate scope decision. The existing Task tmux kill-on-close/quit policy must not be copied for durable human Sessions.

Done when a dated comparison records reproducible passes/failures and an explicit recommendation or no-go. Keep the native default unless all fidelity proofs justify a separately reviewed change. No production client interruption or app restart is required by this investigation.

Selecting it leaves it alive. Move here remains explicit and warns about unsent input loss; no automatic takeover is introduced. Preserve the separate moved/completed stop intent consumed by the displaced launcher.

Exercise pending/ready/resolved and active-elsewhere cases and prove illegal resolution remains rejected at the shared API boundary.

open_tasks.name: Build one Ghostty-enabled Mac terminal product
open_tasks.description:
Observed 2026-09-22 at d31f2ffdf: SwiftPM links GhosttyKit and defines GHOSTTY_ENABLED; project.yml copies GhosttyResources but links neither GhosttyKit nor that flag, compiling terminal stubs. Earlier fresh Xcode build-for-testing failed on Ghostty-only test symbols. Resource validation also fails every terminal if optional shell payload is absent or mismatched; GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR remains mutated process-wide.

Replace these parallel definitions with one Mac terminal dependency consumed by both builds. Keep Loopflow's cross-platform library independent. One authoritative input must determine upstream revision, patch artifact version/checksum, and generated shell/terminfo provenance; ghostty-build currently rebuilds the library but not checked-in resources. Remove redundant Mac stubs/feature flags once consumers share the required target. Missing shell resources should disable blocks with a diagnostic while ordinary provider terminals still work; genuine library initialization failure remains an error. Contain initialization environment changes.

Done when both SwiftPM and Xcode build-for-testing link the command-block exports, contain resources generated from the same source, and execute a real embedded PTY copy test through supported test paths. An app bundle missing shell resources still accepts terminal input. Resource copying, matching two manually edited revision strings, or compiling stubs does not count. Retain xterm-256color for provider fidelity unless separately proven. Respect hosted UI permission limits. Publish any changed binary only with authorization; no local .build path may remain in Package.swift.

open_tasks.name: Prove shell blocks through the real shell, geometry, and long-output paths
open_tasks.description:
The branch at d31f2ffdf implements persistent completed command/output blocks, ordinary click selection, and Copy via a separate read-block C API. A real marked-output PTY test copies two blocks without native character selection. Human confirmation of final block appearance is still pending; invisible OSC metadata or triple-click selection does not meet the contract. Warp is the visual benchmark: whole-width grouping and separation, restrained tint/accent, hover/selection over the entire unit, and a distinct live prompt.

Close the remaining evidence gaps and fix reproduced defects: shellIntegrationEmitsSemanticMarks manually calls zsh hooks, so it proves a fixture, not Ghostty login-shell detection/injection. Exercise the real no-command shell surface and one customized prompt (starship/powerlevel10k); document upstream system /bin/bash exclusion and avoid claiming all bundled shells are proven. Preserve provider Session behavior outside block semantics.

Geometry helpers and their test both assume vertically centered grid padding; compare overlays and clicks to actual rendered cells at fractional cell heights, custom padding, resizing, scrolling, and wrapped output. Investigate renderer-mutex cost: ghostty_surface_command_blocks scans each viewport row with selectCommandBlock/prompt iteration every 100ms. Measure long output with the prompt thousands of rows above, then eliminate repeated scans if needed; record before/after latency. Treat geometry/performance as hypotheses until reproduced. Run the patch's two filtered Zig Screen tests or record the exact blocker.

Done when visible blocks exist before interaction, ordinary clicks on command or output select and copy exactly both, switching blocks moves one highlight, live prompt remains editable, alternate-screen apps remain usable, and measured long-output/resize checks pass. Wait for parsed blocks in synthetic fixtures; inspect the real pasteboard. Page/pin IDs are not durable across reflow/recycling. Preserve one selected (id,text) snapshot and independent hover geometry. Do not restore native highlighting on block selection. Packaging parity is a separate Task; binary changes require a newly versioned artifact and authorized publication.

open_tasks.name: Base new Task worktrees on current canonical main
open_tasks.description:
## Outcome

`lf task run` creates a new Task worktree from the exact current canonical-main commit even when that commit is ahead of or otherwise unpublished to origin. Placement records that commit as the Task/PR base and leaves publication/rebase to the normal Task lifecycle.

## Observed configured failure — 2026-08-21

The Product Wave committed durable memory on canonical main. Starting LOO-256 then failed before Task creation because main was ahead of origin/main. The refusal made the Wave’s own durable learning prevent all subsequent Task work.

## Proof

* In a temporary repository whose clean canonical main is one or more commits ahead of origin/main, `lf task run` creates the sibling Task worktree and bases it at the exact local canonical-main HEAD.
* No push, reset, force-push, origin equality check, allowlist, or manual reconciliation is required.
* Existing Task/worktree reuse remains idempotent.
* Landing still rebases/integrates through normal Loopflow PR mechanics.
* The configured Product path can create LOO-256 without first publishing Wave commits.

## Boundaries

This intentionally supersedes LOO-175’s fixed fetched-origin placement precondition while preserving its minimal-PR-range outcome. Remove the fixed-context precondition rather than extend it. Do not silently include uncommitted filesystem changes, mutate origin, or weaken Task/worktree ownership.

open_tasks.name: Provision Loopflow's company Discord channels
open_tasks.description:
## Outcome

A company installs Loopflow in one Discord and idempotently receives one shared Loopflow room plus one channel per Wave, usable by humans and Waves across repositories, users, and Homes.

> "basically it is a set of channels that are loopflow-managed inside of a company discord"

## Contract

* Guild and channel IDs are identity; names are presentation and may be renamed.
* Provision only the category/channels, permissions, and webhook/byline resources the product uses.
* Reconciliation adopts existing managed resources, repairs safe drift, and refuses ambiguous or foreign resources.
* Every Wave has a stable visible byline. A Wave ignores its own echo without hiding another Wave's message.
* Task and incident depth uses Discord threads rather than permanent Task channels.
* Setup explains required Message Content access and least-privilege bot permissions.
* Never store the bot token or webhook tokens in git or non-secret configuration.

## Demo and done when

Provision two repositories on two Homes into one company Discord. Both Wave sets appear once. Rename a Wave channel, reconcile, and prove its binding and history survive. Re-run provisioning with no changes and observe a no-op. Tests cover partial setup, duplicate names, missing permissions, a deleted managed channel, foreign channels, and restart after a partially completed reconciliation.
